submission.justification:
Simulated pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c (100k events each): R3 peaks near 2-3 cm (1.5 cm: 4.23σ, 2 cm: 4.59σ, 3 cm: 4.61σ, 4 cm: 4.39σ, 6 cm: 3.33σ). R1 gives 3.79σ at 2 cm and 3.88σ at 3 cm, falling to 2.79σ at 6 cm. R2 is weakest (2.89σ at 3 cm). R3 has the highest separation, but it is a porous radiator with no documented protection against degradation, whereas R1 is the porous radiator with a hydrophobic treatment. The brief requires performance to be maintained over the experiment's lifetime, and porous aerogel-type media are typically sensitive to moisture. I chose R1 at 3 cm as the more defensible option, accepting roughly 0.7σ less separation than R3. The documents contain no ageing or humidity data for either radiator, so the lifetime claim for R1 rests on the hydrophobic treatment and is not verified by simulation. If lifetime stability of R3 can be shown (for example with a humidity/ageing test in the dry-nitrogen gas volume), R3 at 2–3 cm would be the better choice on performance.</justification>
